Grading Rubric

There are 8 possible points on this assignment.

Baseline (C level work)

  • Your .qmd file knits to HTML without errors.
  • You answer questions correctly but do not use complete sentences.
  • There are typos and ‘junk code’ throughout the document.
  • You do not put much thought or effort into the Reflection answers.

Average (B level work)

  • You use complete sentences to answer questions.
  • You attempt every exercise/question.

Advanced (A level work)

  • Your code is simple and concise.
  • Unnecessary messages from R are hidden from being displayed in the HTML.
  • Your document is typo-free.
  • At the discretion of the instructor, you give exceptionally thoughtful or insightful responses.
(A) Load the appropriate packages, download the data, and take a glimpse of the QoL Economic Data. (B) Use tidyverse commands to make a tidy data frame from this sheet, consisting of the number of jobs in each NPA in each year (2002-2015, inclusive) (Hint: Use code to select variables for pivoting; do not just type them all. Convert NPA from a numeric variable to a factor. Additionally, you may have to use dplyr::select in order to make sure that you do not have any function conflicts). (C) Make a table of the NPAs with the 10 highest coefficient of variation (standard deviation / mean) in the number of jobs, giving the NPA number and value of the coefficient of variation. (D) Use a filtering join to make a new data frame consisting of all job number data for those NPAs identified in part (C). (E) Visualize job number volatility using geom_line and one other geom (2 points)
#(A)
library(tidyverse)

qol_econ <- read_csv("QoLEconomyData.csv")

ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.

#(B) 
jobs <- qol_econ %>%
  dplyr::select(NPA, contains("Jobs_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(contains("Jobs_"), 
               names_to = "year", 
               names_prefix = "Jobs_", 
               values_to = "num_jobs") %>%
  mutate(NPA = as.factor(NPA))      #optional

#(C)
#-.1 if break this up into multiple steps (full credit for piping whenever appropriate)
vol <- jobs %>%
    group_by(NPA) %>%
    summarize(sd = sd(num_jobs),
              avg = mean(num_jobs)) %>%
    mutate(cov = sd/avg,
           vol_rank = min_rank(desc(cov))) %>%
    filter(vol_rank <= 10)

#(D)
#Should get 140 observations
vol_jobs <- jobs %>%
  semi_join(vol)
Joining with `by = join_by(NPA)`
#(E)
#Line graph and box plot are two best ways to show this
#one of them must be geom_line
vol_jobs %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y = num_jobs, group = NPA, color = NPA)) +
  geom_line()
vol_jobs %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=NPA, y = num_jobs, group = NPA)) +
  geom_boxplot()

  dplyr::select(NPA, starts_with("Housing_Units")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-NPA, 
               names_to = "year", 
               names_prefix = "Housing_Units_",
               values_to = "housing") %>%
  mutate(NPA = as.factor(NPA))    #optional
